finding: We tested whether covering more query contexts preserves retrospective updates better than retaining only recent sources at the same count. At half copying, context balance lowers squared prediction loss in only 2 of 14 half-retention settings under one order and none under its reversal; quarter retention loses in all 14 under both orders. Independent reconstruction, all 1,120 paired strata and both complete replays verify this supplied-law constructed-method result. Learned provenance, historical process correspondence and human intent remain unestablished.
